title: Mulligan Concept: Mobilisation with Movement (MWM) and SNAGs
lead: Pain-free movement with a sustained glide.

book.title: Mulligan Concept: Mobilisation with Movement (MWM) and SNAGs
book.lead: Pain-free movement with a sustained glide.

blocks.text: Brian Mulligan's approach combines a sustained passive accessory glide by the therapist with active movement by the patient. The aim is immediate pain-free movement. Techniques are guided by the **PILL** principle:

items: **P**ain-free: the technique must not cause pain.

blocks.text: The original explanation of correcting a "positional fault" is not proven; effects are likely neurophysiological [Ref – to verify].

rows: Painful limited neck rotation or extension

Patient sits; therapist's thumb (or edge of hand) on the spinous or articular process; glide along the facet plane (toward the eyes); patient actively moves while the glide is held; return to start before releasing
Patient sits or stands with a belt around the pelvis; therapist glides the spinous process along the facet plane while the patient bends
Patient supine, elbow extended; belt or hand applies lateral glide to the forearm near the elbow; patient grips
Patient lunges forward with a belt or hand gliding the tibia forward over the talus (or talus posterior)
Posterolateral glide of the humeral head while the patient elevates

blocks.text: Typically 6 to 10 repetitions, 3 sets, if the PILL response is present. Self-SNAGs with a towel or belt for home practice.

items: If movement is still painful during the technique, change the glide direction, force or location.
If still painful after adjustments, the technique is not indicated: choose another approach.
**What does PILL stand for?** Pain-free, Instant, Long-lasting.
**What do you do if a SNAG is painful?** Adjust glide direction, force or position; abandon if still painful.
**Why add home self-SNAGs?** To maintain and extend the effect between sessions.
**What is the plane of a cervical SNAG?** Along the facet plane, roughly toward the eyes.
**Which MWM is used for lateral elbow pain?** Lateral glide of the forearm with gripping.
